arch.title: Validation Architecture
arch.para: This chapter describes the seven-layer validation architecture implemented in this project. Each layer serves a specific purpose and builds upon the previous layers.

section.title: Layer 0: Maven POM
section.para: The Maven POM (Project Object Model) is the foundation of our validation architecture. It defines:

listitem.para: Resource paths for schemas and catalogs

section.para: The pom.xml is always validated first, ensuring the foundation is sound before any other validation proceeds.

section.title: Layer 1: DTD Validation
section.para: Document Type Definition (DTD) validation provides legacy compatibility and basic structural validation. While older than other schema languages, DTD validation remains important for:

listitem.para: Backward compatibility with existing DocBook 4.x documents

section.title: Layer 2: W3C XSD Validation
section.para: XML Schema (XSD) is the W3C standard for schema validation. It provides:

section.title: Layer 3: RELAX NG Validation
section.para: RELAX NG (Regular Language Description for XML New Generation) is an ISO standard (19757-2) that provides expressive pattern-based validation. Key features include:

listitem.para: Powerful pattern matching with named patterns

section.para: Our constraint schemas add project-specific validation rules on top of the base DocBook 5.2 schema.

section.title: Layer 4: Schematron Validation
section.para: Schematron is an ISO standard (19757-3) for rule-based validation. Unlike other schema languages that describe structure, Schematron describes rules that content must satisfy. This makes it ideal for:

example.title: Schematron Rule Example
example.programlisting: <pattern id="chapter-title-required"> <title>Chapter must have a title</title> <rule context="db:chapter"> <assert test="db:title" severity="error"> Chapter must have a title element </assert> </rule> </pattern>
